items.q: In hepatopulmonary syndrome (HPS), chronic liver disease leads to excessive pulmonary production of which potent gaseous vasodilator?
items.exp: Chronic liver disease stimulates excess nitric oxide (NO) production, resulting in intrapulmonary capillary dilatation. (Book p1009)

items.q: In hepatopulmonary syndrome, what is the extent of intrapulmonary capillary dilatation compared to normal pulmonary capillary diameter?
items.exp: Pulmonary capillary diameter expands dramatically from normal 8-15 µm up to 50-500 µm in HPS. (Book p1009)

items.q: The marked intrapulmonary capillary dilatation in HPS leads to decreased oxygenation and arteriovenous shunts, causing hypoxia/hypoxemia via ________.
items.exp: The combination of decreased oxygenation and AV shunts causes hypoxia/hypoxemia through ventilation-perfusion (V/Q) mismatch. (Book p1009)

items.q: Platypnea is defined as dyspnea provoked by standing upright. What are the two physiological factors identified in the text that produce platypnea in HPS?
opts: Increased AV shunt activation and diaphragm moving up
Decreased bronchial caliber and left ventricular failure
Carotid sinus denervation and alveolar collapse
Pulmonary capillary constriction and diaphragm descent
items.exp: Platypnea is dyspnea on standing due to: (1) ↑ AV shunt activation and (2) diaphragm moves up. (Book p1009)

items.q: Orthodeoxia is a hallmark clinical sign of hepatopulmonary syndrome defined by which specific arterial oxygen saturation change on standing?
items.exp: Orthodeoxia is explicitly defined as a drop of SpO2 > 3% on standing. (Book p1009)

items.q: What is the investigation of choice (IOC) to demonstrate intrapulmonary vascular dilatations in hepatopulmonary syndrome?
opts: Invasive right heart catheterization with pulmonary angiography
items.exp: The investigation of choice (IOC) for HPS is Bubble Echocardiography / Contrast Transthoracic Echocardiography. (Book p1009)

items.q: What is the definitive curative treatment for hepatopulmonary syndrome (HPS)?
items.exp: The definitive treatment for HPS is liver transplantation. (Book p1009)

items.q: A 50-year-old woman with cirrhosis complains of progressive shortness of breath when sitting up, improving when lying flat. Pulse oximetry reveals SpO2 of 96% supine, dropping to 91% on standing. Bubble echocardiography is positive for intrapulmonary shunting. What is the diagnosis and definitive management?
opts: Portopulmonary hypertension; Sildenafil and bosentan therapy
Hepatorenal syndrome type 1; Terlipressin and albumin infusion
Large hepatic hydrothorax; Tube thoracostomy and chemical pleurodesis
items.exp: The triad of chronic liver disease, platypnea-orthodeoxia (drop in SpO2 > 3% on standing), and positive bubble echocardiography confirms hepatopulmonary syndrome (HPS), for which the definitive treatment is liver transplantation. (Book p1009)
